nvcc_profiles./usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc.profile:
TOP              = $(_HERE_)/..

CICC_PATH        = $(TOP)/nvvm-next/bin
NVVMIR_LIBRARY_DIR = $(TOP)/nvvm/libdevice

LD_LIBRARY_PATH += $(TOP)/lib:
PATH            += $(CICC_PATH):$(_HERE_):

INCLUDES        +=  "-I$(TOP)/$(_TARGET_DIR_)/include" $(_SPACE_)
SYSTEM_INCLUDES +=  "-isystem" "$(TOP)/$(_TARGET_DIR_)/include/cccl" $(_SPACE_)

LIBRARIES        =+ $(_SPACE_) "-L$(TOP)/$(_TARGET_DIR_)/lib$(_TARGET_SIZE_)/stubs" "-L$(TOP)/$(_TARGET_DIR_)/lib$(_TARGET_SIZE_)"

CUDAFE_FLAGS    +=
PTXAS_FLAGS     +=

probe.pch_help:
Specify options directly to library manager.

--pch                                               --pch                       
        Enable precompiled header (PCH) processing. When specified, each compilation
        searches the PCH directory (see --pch-dir) for a reusable precompiled header,
        and creates a new one when none is found.

--pch-dir <directory>                               --pch-dir <directory>       
        Specify the directory in which precompiled header files are read from and
        written to. By default this is the current working directory. Ignored unless
        --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--pch-verbose                                       --pch-verbose               
        Print (to stderr) messages related to precompiled header processing. Ignored
        unless --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--create-pch <name>                                 --create-pch <name>         
        Manually create a precompiled header (PCH) at the first PCH terminal stop-point
        (i.e., #pragma hdrstop) and save it under the specified name. Intermediate
        stop points (#pragma hdrstop++) are ignored. The directory into which the
        PCH file is written is determined by --pch-dir (or is the current working
        directory if not specified). This option forces a PCH file to be created
        (any existing PCH file with the same name is overwritten). This option is
        mutually exclusive with '--use-pch' and '--pch'.

--use-pch <name>                                    --use-pch <name>            
        If a precompiled header (PCH) with the specified name exists in the directory
        determined by '--pch-dir' (or the current working directory if not specified),
        try to use it in compilation.This option is mutually exclusive with '--create-pch'
        and '--pch'.

--ptxas-options <options>,...                       (-Xptxas)                   
        Specify options directly to ptxas, the PTX optimizing assembler.

--nvlink-options <options>,...                      (-Xnvlink)                  
        Specify options directly to nvlink.

--nvprune-options <options>,...                     (-Xnvprune)                 
        Specify options directly to nvprune (used with -prune).


Miscellaneous options for guiding the compiler driver.
======================================================

probe.pch_help:
Specify options directly to library manager.

--pch                                               --pch                       
        Enable precompiled header (PCH) processing. When specified, each compilation
        searches the PCH directory (see --pch-dir) for a reusable precompiled header,
        and creates a new one when none is found.

--pch-dir <directory>                               --pch-dir <directory>       
        Specify the directory in which precompiled header files are read from and
        written to. By default this is the current working directory. Ignored unless
        --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--pch-verbose                                       --pch-verbose               
        Print (to stderr) messages related to precompiled header processing. Ignored
        unless --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--create-pch <name>                                 --create-pch <name>         
        Manually create a precompiled header (PCH) at the first PCH terminal stop-point
        (i.e., #pragma hdrstop) and save it under the specified name. Intermediate
        stop points (#pragma hdrstop++) are ignored. The directory into which the
        PCH file is written is determined by --pch-dir (or is the current working
        directory if not specified). This option forces a PCH file to be created
        (any existing PCH file with the same name is overwritten). This option is
        mutually exclusive with '--use-pch' and '--pch'.

--use-pch <name>                                    --use-pch <name>            
        If a precompiled header (PCH) with the specified name exists in the directory
        determined by '--pch-dir' (or the current working directory if not specified),
        try to use it in compilation.This option is mutually exclusive with '--create-pch'
        and '--pch'.

--ptxas-options <options>,...                       (-Xptxas)                   
        Specify options directly to ptxas, the PTX optimizing assembler.

--nvlink-options <options>,...                      (-Xnvlink)                  
        Specify options directly to nvlink.

--nvprune-options <options>,...                     (-Xnvprune)                 
        Specify options directly to nvprune (used with -prune).


Miscellaneous options for guiding the compiler driver.
======================================================

probe.pch_help:
Specify options directly to library manager.

--pch                                               --pch                       
        Enable precompiled header (PCH) processing. When specified, each compilation
        searches the PCH directory (see --pch-dir) for a reusable precompiled header,
        and creates a new one when none is found.

--pch-dir <directory>                               --pch-dir <directory>       
        Specify the directory in which precompiled header files are read from and
        written to. By default this is the current working directory. Ignored unless
        --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--pch-verbose                                       --pch-verbose               
        Print (to stderr) messages related to precompiled header processing. Ignored
        unless --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--create-pch <name>                                 --create-pch <name>         
        Manually create a precompiled header (PCH) at the first PCH terminal stop-point
        (i.e., #pragma hdrstop) and save it under the specified name. Intermediate
        stop points (#pragma hdrstop++) are ignored. The directory into which the
        PCH file is written is determined by --pch-dir (or is the current working
        directory if not specified). This option forces a PCH file to be created
        (any existing PCH file with the same name is overwritten). This option is
        mutually exclusive with '--use-pch' and '--pch'.

--use-pch <name>                                    --use-pch <name>            
        If a precompiled header (PCH) with the specified name exists in the directory
        determined by '--pch-dir' (or the current working directory if not specified),
        try to use it in compilation.This option is mutually exclusive with '--create-pch'
        and '--pch'.

--ptxas-options <options>,...                       (-Xptxas)                   
        Specify options directly to ptxas, the PTX optimizing assembler.

--nvlink-options <options>,...                      (-Xnvlink)                  
        Specify options directly to nvlink.

--nvprune-options <options>,...                     (-Xnvprune)                 
        Specify options directly to nvprune (used with -prune).


Miscellaneous options for guiding the compiler driver.

probe.pch_help:
Specify options directly to library manager.

--pch                                               --pch                       
        Enable precompiled header (PCH) processing. When specified, each compilation
        searches the PCH directory (see --pch-dir) for a reusable precompiled header,
        and creates a new one when none is found.

--pch-dir <directory>                               --pch-dir <directory>       
        Specify the directory in which precompiled header files are read from and
        written to. By default this is the current working directory. Ignored unless
        --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--pch-verbose                                       --pch-verbose               
        Print (to stderr) messages related to precompiled header processing. Ignored
        unless --pch, --create-pch, or --use-pch is enabled.

--create-pch <name>                                 --create-pch <name>         
        Manually create a precompiled header (PCH) at the first PCH terminal stop-point
        (i.e., #pragma hdrstop) and save it under the specified name. Intermediate
        stop points (#pragma hdrstop++) are ignored. The directory into which the
        PCH file is written is determined by --pch-dir (or is the current working
        directory if not specified). This option forces a PCH file to be created
        (any existing PCH file with the same name is overwritten). This option is
        mutually exclusive with '--use-pch' and '--pch'.

--use-pch <name>                                    --use-pch <name>            
        If a precompiled header (PCH) with the specified name exists in the directory
        determined by '--pch-dir' (or the current working directory if not specified),
        try to use it in compilation.This option is mutually exclusive with '--create-pch'
        and '--pch'.

--ptxas-options <options>,...                       (-Xptxas)                   
        Specify options directly to ptxas, the PTX optimizing assembler.

--nvlink-options <options>,...                      (-Xnvlink)                  
        Specify options directly to nvlink.

--nvprune-options <options>,...                     (-Xnvprune)                 
        Specify options directly to nvprune (used with -prune).


Miscellaneous options for guiding the compiler driver.
======================================================
